compiled_state.title: [Sprint orchestrator]: Sub-agent worktrees auto-cleaned before harvest -> implementation work lost
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Incident Overview

**Expected behavior**: When a sub-agent dispatched with `isolation: "worktree"` completes successfully (STATUS: pass), the agent's worktree should persist with committed changes until the sprint orchestrator harvests them via `per-worktree-review-commit.md`.

**Actual behavior**: Sub-agent worktrees are auto-cleaned immediately on agent completion. The platform removes the worktree directory when the agent process ends, regardless of whether changes were committed. All file modifications made by the agent are lost.

**Impact**: Sprint Batch 1 (spike task), Batch 2 (contract doc, lint wrapper, negative directive) — all 4 sub-agents completed successfully but their worktrees were removed before harvest. The orchestrator resorted to direct implementation (HARD-GATE violation) as a workaround.

## Technical Environment

- Platform: darwin (macOS 25.5.0)
- Claude Code version: Opus 4.7 (1M context)
- Worktree isolation: enabled (default)
- Sprint mode: ci-pr

## Action History

1. Sprint orchestrator dispatched spike task with `isolation: "worktree"`, `run_in_background: true`
2. Sub-agent ran for ~600s, created files, reported STATUS: pass
3. Orchestrator checked `git worktree list` — worktree was `locked`
4. Orchestrator checked files in worktree — worktree directory was gone
5. Pattern repeated for 3 more sub-agents in Batch 2

## Reproduction

Dispatch any sub-agent with `isolation: "worktree"` and `run_in_background: true`. After the agent completes, check `git worktree list` — the worktree entry will be absent. The platform auto-cleans worktrees on agent completion regardless of whether the agent committed changes.

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The Claude Code platform's worktree lifecycle management removes the worktree when the agent process ends. The `per-worktree-review-commit.md` protocol assumes worktrees persist until the orchestrator explicitly harvests them via `harvest-worktree.sh`, but the platform cleans them first.

Possible factors:
- The platform may auto-clean worktrees that have no new commits (no changes = auto-remove)
- Sub-agents may not be committing their work within the worktree before reporting completion
- The task-execution.md template may lack explicit commit instructions for worktree-isolated agents

## Skills and Workflows

- Sprint SKILL.md Phase E (Sub-Agent Launch) — dispatches with `isolation: "worktree"`
- Sprint SKILL.md Phase F — per-worktree-review-commit.md protocol assumes worktree persists
- task-execution.md — sub-agent task template; may lack commit instructions

comments.body:
INVESTIGATION COMPLETE — Two-layer root cause confirmed via probes:

Layer 1 (PRIMARY): Sprint orchestrator injected session-worktree absolute paths into sub-agent prompts. Agents used those paths in Read/Edit/Write tool calls, causing changes to land in the session worktree instead of the agent's isolated worktree. The isolated worktree had no changes → platform correctly auto-cleaned it.

Layer 2 (SECONDARY): task-execution.md lacks a git add -A step before reporting. Even with correct paths, unstaged changes may not trigger the platform's worktree retention signal. Probe 2 confirmed: staging files preserves the worktree.

Proposed 3-part fix:
A) Orchestrator prompt discipline — remove absolute session paths from sub-agent prompts
B) task-execution.md — add git add -A before Step 9 (report output)
C) Phase F 907d recovery — check session worktree for uncommitted changes when isolated WT is auto-cleaned
comments.author: Test

comments.body: Fixed via PR #399 (merged). Two changes: (1) task-execution.md Step 8b adds git add -A for worktree retention, (2) Sprint SKILL.md Phase E adds prompt path hygiene rule. Additionally, per-worktree-review-commit.md updated to clean up on exit 3 (empty branch) and 907d orphan branches.
